License is informal: these are freely-redistributable test binaries with no formal license file, recorded as unknown; author site http://www.slack.net/~ant/. All 18 ROMs are committed and all 18 currently PASS in this emulator with visually-approved screen-CRC goldens, one test per ROM (blargg_rom_test! in blargg_apu_tests.rs). timer_at_power_reset requires a mid-test soft reset when the ROM jumps to $0000 (modeled via RunConfig::with_reset_on_pc_trap); spc_dsp6 needs an extended 600M-tick budget and runs to frame 9100. assets.notes: undisbeliever (Marcus Rowe) SNES hardware-glitch/timing-hammer test ROMs. Unlike blargg/gilyon, these do not print a PASS/FAIL text screen -- most demonstrate a real, documented hardware bug (the 'INIDISP D7 glitch': writing $2100 shortly after the CPU/HDMA data bus held a byte with bit 7 set can corrupt sprite rendering or briefly flip force-blank on real 3-chip/1-chip consoles; see the NESdev post quoted at https://github.com/akatsuki105/snes-test-roms/tree/master/undisbeliever-inidisp, from Near/byuu, with real-hardware reference photos) or are interactive demos. No known SNES emulator models this glitch -- checked Mesen2, ares (Near's own current emulator), and Snes9x, all write $2100 deterministically with no bus-residual modeling (issue #2949). All 29 vendored ROMs are automated, each a 0-pixel byte-for-byte match against a Mesen2 capture of the same frame (--Video.VideoFilter=None --Video.AspectRatio=NoStretching --snes.disableFrameSkipping=true, diffed with python -m scripts.diff_screenshots). NESER and Mesen2 align at zero row offset: the 'harmless constant 1-scanline row offset' this manifest previously claimed was in fact a NESER BG vertical-scroll bug, fixed in #2945/#2981, so a non-zero best shift is now evidence of a bug rather than a convention to allow for. 14 of the 29 belong to the D7-glitch family. For 3 of those (hdma-21ff-glitch.sfc, inidisp_hammer_0f0f.sfc, hdma-2100-glitch-2ch-0a.sfc) the source confirms real hardware never glitches, so those goldens genuinely are hardware-accurate; for the other 11 (hdma-2100-glitch.sfc, hdma-2100-glitch-2ch-81.sfc, hdma-21ff-2100-0f-glitch.sfc, hdma-21ff-2100-glitch.sfc, inidisp_d7_glitch_test.sfc, inidisp_hammer_0f.sfc, inidisp_hammer_0f00.sfc, inidisp_hammer_0f8f.sfc, inidisp_hammer_0f8f_fast.sfc, inidisp_hammer_0f_long.sfc, inidisp_hammer_8f0f.sfc) real hardware usually glitches and the golden only proves parity with a limitation shared by every checked reference emulator (issue #2949), not hardware accuracy. The remaining 15 (hdmaen_latch_test(_2).sfc, inidisp_brightness_delay.sfc, inidisp_enable_display_mid_frame.sfc, inidisp_forgot_to_force_blank.sfc, and the 10 scpu-a-dma-bug-*.sfc) are unrelated to the D7 glitch and are confirmed Mesen2-exact. The last 3 to be automated (hdma-2100-glitch-2ch-{0a,81}.sfc, hdma-21ff-2100-glitch.sfc) were held back under #2943/#3083 until their HDMA banding phase matched; it does as of #3062. See snes::integration_tests::undisbeliever_tests and README-SNES.md.

Neither prints a PASS/FAIL text screen; both are cross-checked against Mesen2 captures of the identical ROM file, same methodology as the undisbeliever suite. 1 of 2 is automated: hvdma.sfc (all 8 HDMA channels force-blank/write-VRAM-address/burst-20-bytes/unblank on two scanlines, changing BG1's tile pattern partway down the screen) now matches both Mesen2 and the bundled real-hardware reference photo after fixing #2952 (NESER's HDMA transfer mode 5 was reusing general-purpose DMA's cyclic-mode simplification, truncating 4 bytes/line to 2 and desyncing the per-channel HDMA table pointer, so every VMDATA channel mistook a leftover data byte for the table terminator right after its first line). hvdma_max.sfc (an H-IRQ-triggered DMA burst probing force-blank release timing) renders solid black in NESER vs. Mesen2's documented solid green -- a real, separate rendering gap unaffected by the #2952 fix, tracked as #2953 and deliberately left un-automated. assets.notes: KungFuFurby's 2005-2008 NMI/H-V-IRQ test ROM collection (issue #2883/#3049, epic #2724), posted on the nesdev forum in 2016 (informal find, no LICENSE file, recorded as unknown). Blue backdrop = PASS, red/maroon = FAIL. Both suites self-check by capturing the opcode byte at the interrupted PC via a stack-relative-indirect-indexed LDA off the auto-pushed interrupt frame and comparing it against the expected in-flight opcode. demo_nmitest.smc, nmi.smc and demo_irqtest.smc match Mesen2 exactly and carry approved goldens (snes::integration_tests::kungfufurby_nmi_tests / kungfufurby_irq_tests) after #3049's per-CPU-cycle NMI and H/V-IRQ dispatch fixes (Cpu::step() now checks interrupt-pending state at per-cycle rather than per-instruction granularity, mirroring Mesen2's DetectNmiSignalEdge/PrevIrqSource); test_nmi.smc and test_irq4209.smc pass since #3116 made STP halt the CPU, and test_irq4200.smc since #3144 ported Mesen2's level+edge IRQ counter circuit. test_irq.smc (#3146, dispatch boundary one instruction early), test_irqb.smc (#3147, open-bus OPHCT latch 4 dots low) and irq.smc (no source; re-measured once #3146 lands) remain #[ignore]d under the #3093 tracker, asserting the Mesen2-correct PASS goldens per the #3092 convention. test_irq.smc and test_irq4200.smc are byte-identical to the tukuyomi-bsnes-tests mirror copies of the same names; nmi.smc is byte-identical to jonasquinn-test-roms' nmi_irq/nmi.smc. tukuyomi's test_nmi.smc/demo_nmitest.smc/demo_irqtest.smc and jonasquinn's nmi_irq/demo_nmi.smc, demo_irq.smc and nmi_pf/test_nmi.smc are different revisions despite matching or similar names (sha256-verified) and remain documented-only candidates, not separately automated. snes_test_tsc.smc remains out of scope. The HDMA ROMs test_hdma.smc, test_hdmasync.smc and test_hdmatiming.smc are now automated in snes::integration_tests::kungfufurby_hdma_tests (issue #2884) as #[ignore]d divergences: test_hdma/test_hdmasync render black and test_hdmatiming FAILs (red) where Mesen2 PASSes (blue), rooted in HDMA H-position timing (#3062, #3042/#3050).

assets.notes: Sour/SnesTests' dma_irq_test.sfc (issue #2883/#3049, epic #2724): validates how many instructions run after a manual DMA ($420B write) before a pending IRQ or NMI dispatches, across 19 sub-cases rendered as text. Rebuilt byte-identical from source (ca65 -g + ld65 --dbgfile, sha256-verified against the vendored .sfc) to recover the WRAM result-table address from the debug symbol table. The upstream README's expected-results table has a transcription error (lists $FFFF for the two SEI+INC no-interrupt sub-cases; the real, Mesen2-confirmed sentinel is $00FF, since the captured byte is a single-byte WRAM location written via an 8-bit STA) -- the golden CRC reflects the Mesen2-verified screen, not the README table. NESER originally diverged on 8/19 sub-cases, each off by exactly one fewer dispatched instruction than Mesen2 -- the same interrupt-dispatch-precision signature tracked in #3049 (see snes-tests-kungfufurby-nmi-irq). #3049's per-cycle NMI/IRQ dispatch fixes closed 2 of those 8 (both CLI+INC sub-cases) and #3065 closed the remaining 6; both tests are active (the 19-value WRAM oracle plus the Mesen2-verified frame-600 screen CRC), and the mechanism was later simplified by #3074 (per-cycle DMA interrupt lock) and #3081 (instruction-granular irq_lock_step deleted) without moving any value. op_timing_test (65816 opcode cycle-count validation, a CPU-timing concern rather than IRQ/NMI/DMA) and timing_test (upstream README: 'WIP... attempts to validate rough timings', no stable oracle) are vendored in the same source tree but out of scope and remain documented-only candidates for future work.

assets.notes: Deterministic in-code assembled LoROM fixture programs (fixture_rom.rs) for general-purpose DMA (issue #2884), authored against the fullsnes register spec without reading the DMA implementation. Black-box, end-to-end: real 65816 code arms $43xx/$420B, the real PPU runs the transfer, and the result is read back through the actual B-bus target path. Covers mode 0/1 A->B to WRAM (via WMDATA) and VRAM, palette to CGRAM, words to OAM, A-bus increment/decrement/fixed, byte-count 0 == 65536, ascending multi-channel priority, and #2944 active-display write gating. VRAM/CGRAM/OAM readback instruments are each proven by a CPU write/read self-check. Pass/fail via the rom_runner NSER WRAM marker; no on-disk ROMs or visual baselines. B->A direction (#3061): WMDATA $2180 into cartridge SRAM, and the VRAM read port $2139/$213A into WRAM including its prefetch/increment side effects.

assets.notes: Deterministic in-code SNES cartridge images (issue #2885, epic #2724) for base-cartridge verification, built by cartridge_fixtures.rs and authored from the SNES header spec (fullsnes/nesdev) rather than the loader. Minimal LoROM/HiROM/ExHiROM and copier-header fixtures are loaded through the real Cartridge/bus paths to assert mapping detection, title/country region metadata, SRAM size + battery flags, ROM address translation (a sentinel byte read back at the mapped CPU address for each mapping's banks/halves), and 512-byte copier-header stripping. An executable LoROM battery-SRAM fixture (via the fixture_rom builder) writes two distinct SRAM addresses and reads one back with a CPU self-check, defeating open-bus/MDR false passes and pinning the SRAM read/write decode. No-enhancement-chip cartridges only. Pass/fail via the rom_runner NSER WRAM marker (executable fixture) plus direct Cartridge/debugger assertions; no on-disk ROMs or visual baselines. Complements the header/persistence unit coverage in src/snes/cartridge and src/snes/console/snes.rs.
